summary: High-cardinality trace filter causes dashboard panels to go blank and suppress alert evaluations
description:
Issue summary:
Customer FinNimbus reported dashboards and alerting stopped returning data for certain saved panels after they applied a complex trace filter (~1200 distinct tag values) to the dashboard. Alerts linked to those panels did not evaluate or fire for approximately 4 hours.

Impact:
- Multiple operational dashboards for FinNimbus showed 'No data' for hourly panels between 2026-03-10 02:00-06:00 UTC.
- Two alerting rules based on those panels did not evaluate or trigger, delaying on-call response for an upstream ingestion problem.
- Affected a single enterprise org on Dedicated capacity in eu-west.

Expected behavior:
- Panels should paginate or show sampled results without causing evaluation pipelines to drop. Alerts should either evaluate on sampled results or fail open with a clear error visible in the alert history.

Observed behavior:
- Query planner attempted to expand the filter fanout into thousands of OR clauses, exceeding planner limits. The console front-end received a 204 (no content) from the trace-query service and marked panels as empty. The alert-eval worker treated the empty result as 'skip' and did not mark an error, so no notification was sent.
steps_to_reproduce: Login to FinNimbus org on eu-west dedicated cluster
Open Dashboard 'Ingest Health - Traces' and add a filter on trace.tag.pipeline_id with ~1200 values (multi-select paste)
Save and refresh the dashboard time window covering last 1h
Observe panel shows 'No data' and alert history shows 'No evaluation' instead of an error
logs: 2026-03-10T02:12:08Z trace-query[warn] planner: expanded predicate into 1213 disjuncts, truncating to 1024
2026-03-10T02:12:08Z console[error] panel-render: trace-query returned empty result (status=204) for query id=fd3a1b
2026-03-10T02:12:09Z alert-eval[info] evaluation-skip: panel result empty, rule_id=alertrule-37, org=finimbus
2026-03-10T02:12:09Z scheduler[debug] enqueue-eval: rule marked as skipped (no error), eval_id=eval-20260310-0212
comments: 2026-03-10 Priya Shah (support): Customer reported missing dashboard metrics and missed alerts after applying a large multi-value filter. Provided initial screenshots and alert IDs.

2026-03-10 Marco Ruiz (on-call SRE): Acknowledged, started investigation. Confirmed the customer is on Dedicated eu-west. Spun up query logs and reproduced a similar filter locally against a staging ingest snapshot.

2026-03-10 Alyssa Chen (runtime): Hypothesis: query planner truncation combined with alert-eval treating empty result as skip. Adding to investigation. Linking to PR that touches planner predicate limits: https://github.com/redwood-inference/query-engine/pull/8123

2026-03-11 Marco Ruiz (SRE): Deployed a short-term mitigation: alert-eval will now treat 204 as an error for org-scoped evaluations (rollout id: rollout-2026-03-11-plain). Asked customer to remove the giant IN filter as a temporary workaround.

2026-03-12 Priya Shah (support): Customer confirmed removing the large filter restored panel data and alerts fired for subsequent incidents. Customer requested a permanent fix to avoid having to trim filters.
2026-03-13 Marco Ruiz (SRE): Root cause identified and fixed; backported PR merged. Notified customer and closed ticket after validation.
investigation_notes:
Summary of findings: The trace-query planner has a hard cap on predicate expansion to protect downstream query engines. When a large multi-value tag filter is pasted, we expand it into OR chains; beyond 1024 disjuncts we truncate and return an empty result to avoid expensive execution. The console UI surfaces this as No Data (204). Alert-eval historically treated empty results as a benign 'skip' rather than a failure, so rules were not retried or escalated.

Sequence: user saved dashboard with a high-cardinality IN() filter -> planner expansion hit truncation threshold -> trace-query returned empty payload (status 204) -> console rendered empty panel -> alert-eval read the empty payload and skipped evaluation -> no alert triggered.

Temporary mitigation: changed alert-eval to flag 204 as an evaluation error for org-scoped rules and added logging so skipped evaluations are visible in alert history. Also added UI messaging to dashboards: when a query truncation event occurs, show a warning and a link to recommended best-practices.
resolution:
Fixes applied:
1) Query-engine PR #8123: increased predicate expansion limit and implemented a safe fallback that returns sampled results instead of empty when truncation occurs (merged and backported to 2026-03-11 release branch).
2) Alert-eval change: treat 204/empty-results as explicit errors for evaluation pipelines, causing retries and on-call notifications (rollout-2026-03-11).
3) Console UX change: surfaced a clear warning for truncated/high-cardinality filters and included 'Reduce cardinality' guidance.
4) Customer guidance: advised FinNimbus to use tag whitelisting or apply regex-based grouping instead of pasting thousands of tag values.

Post-deployment validation: FinNimbus confirmed on 2026-03-12 that dashboards returned expected series and alerts triggered for a simulated ingestion outage. No recurrence observed through 2026-03-13. Ticket closed with customer agreement to upgrade their saved filters to the recommended pattern.
